title: PTM-Driven Reshaping of the Peptide Translocation Landscape in Bilayer Graphene Nanopores.
authors: Upadhyaya, Anurag; Sur, Pranjal; Varma, Manoj; Maiti, Prabal K
journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
one_liner_zh: 该文利用全原子分子动力学模拟研究PTM修饰对p53肽段在双层石墨烯纳米孔中易位行为的影响，虽涉及蛋白质-纳米孔互作和分子动力学方法，但核心是肽段易位而非TF-DNA结合与互作机制，仅方法可迁移至蛋白质-DNA互作研究。
abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) underpin much of protein regulation, yet their single-molecule readout remains a challenge in nanopore proteomics. While biological nanopores have shown exquisite PTM sensitivity, the microscopic mechanisms by which PTMs perturb signals in solid-state nanopores are largely unexplored. Here, we use all-atom molecular dynamics to investigate how three common PTMs, acetylation, phosphorylation, and methylation, modulate the translocation of a cancer-relevant p53 peptide fragment through a bilayer graphene nanopore. We find that PTMs remodel the translocation landscape far more strongly at the level of dwell-time statistics than at the level of mean current blockade. Acetylation enhances peptide-graphene adhesion and substantially slows transport, with adjacent acetylations producing the longest residence times due to cooperative interfacial interactions, while remotely spaced acetylations yield broader, heterogeneous dynamics. Phosphorylation introduces a negative charge that increases dwell time through an electrostatic tug-of-war. In contrast, methylation minimally perturbs translocation due to weak pore interactions and preserved charge. Combining dwell time with relative blockade features enables a simple linear SVM classifier to reliably distinguish unmodified, acetylated, and phosphorylated states. These results establish mechanistic design principles for PTM detection using solid-state nanopores and delineate which classes of PTMs are the most amenable to single-molecule detection with these devices.
abstract_zh: 翻译后修饰（PTMs）是蛋白质调控的重要基础，然而在纳米孔蛋白质组学中，其单分子读出仍是一项挑战。尽管生物纳米孔已展现出对PTM的精细敏感性，但PTM在固态纳米孔中扰动信号的微观机制在很大程度上尚未被探索。在此，我们利用全原子分子动力学（all-atom molecular dynamics）研究三种常见PTM——乙酰化（acetylation）、磷酸化（phosphorylation）和甲基化（methylation）——如何调控一个癌症相关的p53肽段片段通过双层石墨烯纳米孔的易位过程。我们发现，PTM在停留时间统计层面重塑易位景观的强度远大于在平均电流阻断层面。乙酰化增强肽段与石墨烯的粘附并显著减缓运输，相邻乙酰化因协同界面相互作用产生最长的停留时间，而间隔较远的乙酰化则导致更宽泛、异质的动力学行为。磷酸化引入负电荷，通过静电拉锯战增加停留时间。相比之下，甲基化因与孔相互作用弱且电荷保持不变，对易位的扰动最小。将停留时间与相对阻断特征相结合，可使一个简单的线性SVM分类器可靠地区分未修饰、乙酰化和磷酸化状态。这些结果为利用固态纳米孔检测PTM建立了机制性设计原则，并阐明了哪些类别的PTM最适用于这些器件的单分子检测。
